title: Flock Wants a Closely Surveilled World with No Exit
summary: The New Yorker article examines Flock Safety, a surveillance technology company that provides license plate readers and AI-powered cameras to neighborhoods and law enforcement, creating an extensive surveillance network that critics argue removes any possibility of anonymity in public spaces.
problem_solved: From Flock's perspective: enabling communities to track vehicles and reduce crime; from critics' view: creating persistent surveillance infrastructure with no opt-out for citizens.
why_valuable: This article raises critical questions about the privacy-surveillance tradeoff as AI-powered surveillance becomes increasingly ubiquitous in American neighborhoods.
